title: Semantics of Programming Languages
description: Formal semantics of programs: abstract machines (SECD and the λ-calculus), operational, denotational and axiomatic semantics, Hoare logic, basic program analysis and program transformation.

topics.title: Semantics and Abstract Machines
topics.summary: Formal semantics rigorously specifies what programs mean, revealing ambiguities in language manuals and giving a basis for implementation and proofs of correctness. Abstract machines such as Landin's SECD machine, with its Stack, Environment, Control and Dump, give step-by-step meaning to languages like the λ-calculus.
subtopics: Why formal semantics; syntax versus semantics
Abstract machines: memory and interpreter; the SMC machine
Types of abstract machine: WAM, SECD, RAM, LAM, CHAM and others
The SECD machine: Stack, Environment, Control and Dump
λ-calculus expressions: names, functions and applications
SECD initial and final states

topics.title: Operational and Denotational Semantics
topics.summary: Operational semantics gives a construct's meaning as the computation it induces on a machine, while denotational semantics maps each piece of syntax to a mathematical object that represents only its effect. A denotational definition has syntactic categories, BNF, semantic domains, semantic functions and semantic equations, and it is compositional.
subtopics: Three ways to describe meaning: operational, denotational, axiomatic
Operational semantics: structural (small-step) and big-step (natural)
Denotational semantics: meaning maps syntax to semantics
The five parts of a denotational definition
Semantic domains (Boolean, Integer, Store) and semantic functions
Compositionality, direct style and fixed-point semantics

topics.title: Axiomatic Semantics and Hoare Logic
topics.summary: Axiomatic program verification proves with mathematics that a program meets its specification, using preconditions, postconditions, invariants and proof obligations. Tony Hoare's 1969 logic expresses this as triples {P} S {Q}, proved with the assignment, sequence and conditional rules.
subtopics: Why testing alone cannot show the absence of bugs
Formal specifications, assertions and proof obligations
Hoare triples {P} S {Q} and checking validity
Assignment, sequence and conditional rules
Partial and total correctness
Dynamic logic and separation logic

topics.title: Basic Program Analysis
topics.summary: Program analysis systematically examines programs to understand their behaviour, correctness and performance, statically without running them or dynamically while they run. Static analysis covers syntax, type, control flow and data flow analysis; dynamic analysis covers testing, profiling and program slicing.
subtopics: What program analysis is and why it matters
Static analysis: linting, type checking, complexity metrics
Control flow analysis and control flow graphs
Data flow analysis: def-use, reaching definitions, live variables
Dynamic analysis: dynamic testing, program slicing, profiling
Tools: LLVM, GCC, SonarQube, Clang Static Analyzer, FindBugs, Valgrind

topics.title: Program Transformation
topics.summary: A program transformation takes a program and produces another while preserving its intended behaviour, for refactoring, optimization, translation, specialisation or obfuscation. Common techniques include AST manipulation, term rewriting, loop unrolling, constant folding, inlining and data structure transformation.
subtopics: Kinds of transformation and why they matter
History: Burstall and Darlington's unfold/fold, refactoring
Techniques: AST manipulation, term rewriting, pattern matching, slicing, symbolic execution
Source-to-source transformation (transpilation)
Refactoring versus optimization; loop unrolling, constant folding, inlining
High-level versus low-level transformation; challenges
